Prevention: This is a migratory pest; and therefore it is difficult to prevent the pest problem as they immigrate from outside to your fields.
Surround or rotate maize fields with cotton or flowering crops such as alfalfa which locusts do not like.
Plant oil crops, such as castor- oil plants to attract natural enemies (such as birds) against locusts.
Monitoring: Young migratory locusts are 2.5 to 3.5 cm, and mottled-black with orange marks on sides
Adult migratory locusts are 4 to 8 cm big, pale-brown with black marks, whereas solitary non-migratory adult locust are green to dark green-brown
Search for and count young less than 3 cm locusts in 5 parts of a maize field in the mornings once a week at young and vegetative crop stages.
At less than 10 young locusts per 10 m 2 of young maize capture locusts by sweeping net; or apply biological methods
A more than 50 adult or young locusts/ 10 m
At 10 to 50 young locusts per 10 m 2 , consider chemical control options.
Young locust may come together when ground-moving into fields, and build bands of thousands of locust.
They may be directly targeted for control.
If many swarms of adult locusts invade your field, you cannot do much anymore.

Restrictions: Many young locusts may come together when ground-moving towards a maize field, and build bands of thousands of locust slowly moving.
They may be directly sprayed using knapsack or boom sprayers.
When using a chemical or botanical pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
